entities.name: Non-specific neck pain
observations: Target population in the direct randomized comparison of SNAGs with versus without isometric exercise training.

entities.name: PMID:25097535
observations: Randomized controlled trial in 102 adults with non-specific neck pain comparing SNAGs plus isometric exercise training (n=51) with SNAGs alone (n=51), approximately six weeks.
Reported greater between-group improvement for pain (VAS p=0.013) and disability (NDI p=0.003); SNAG plus exercise NDI changed 40 to 15 versus 42 to 30 with SNAGs alone.
Pain reporting is internally difficult to interpret because both groups were reported as changing from VAS 7 to 4; no cervical ROM, adverse-event, or longer-term follow-up data were reported.

entities.name: PMID:24467843
observations: Randomized clinical trial in 51 completers with mechanically reproducible chronic neck pain comparing SNAGs, HVLA, and mobilization.
No significant between-group differences in pain, disability, global rating, or cervical ROM at treatment completion or 1 to 3 months follow-up.

entities.name: PMID:40439260
observations: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 randomized trials in adults with non-specific neck pain.

Mulligan techniques were generally not superior in acute or mixed-duration neck pain; combined SNAG interventions sometimes outperformed comparators in chronic or unclear-duration populations, but certainty was very low.

entities.name: PMID:24792139
observations: Indirect randomized evidence in chronic cervicogenic dizziness found SNAG-based treatment improved cervical ROM, with greater post-treatment extension and right-rotation gains than passive mobilization; this population differs from non-specific neck pain.

entities.name: SNAG exercise disability benefit
observations: In one direct RCT, adding isometric exercise to SNAGs produced a larger reported NDI improvement than SNAGs alone: 40 to 15 versus 42 to 30; between-group p=0.003.

entities.name: SNAG exercise pain evidence
observations: The direct RCT reported a statistically significant between-group pain result (p=0.013), but both groups were reported to improve from VAS 7 to 4, making the clinical magnitude and reliability uncertain.
